theme: Admitting patients when discharge is the bottleneck
title: Admitting Patients When Discharge Is The Bottleneck: A Specialty-Bed Reserve Policy
strategies: never lend a bed across wards: reserve = capacity every day (reproduces the evaluator's weak baseline reference, ~0.1)
maximize same-day utilization: reserve = 0 every day, always admit an outlier the instant a bed is free -- no forecast use, no notion that a lending ward will need its beds back

turnover-net-demand reserve: shadow-simulate each ward's own home occupancy forward under the public forecast, estimate how much of that occupancy will discharge organically within a lookahead window, and reserve only the forecasted near-term demand NOT already covered by that organic turnover -- collapses to ~0 (full lending) when a ward is quiet, rises ahead of a ward's own demand ramp before it is caught full of slow-discharging outliers

stronger variants: rolling re-optimization of the reserve trajectory against a multi-ward flow relaxation, or a min-cost-flow / LP formulation over the whole horizon using the full forecast and the outlier discharge-rate penalty
